_comment: Reviewed corpus-vacuity records for the cross-language artifact-role parity
gate (datrix/scripts/test/artifact-role-parity-gate.ps1). Each entry names one
(language, domain) coordinate where that language realizes the domain by a
structural_pattern that matches ZERO paths anywhere in
that language's ENTIRE generated footprint -- every registered example's tree under
<workspace>/.generated/<language>/, read from the pipeline's own manifests.
The gate SKIPS such a domain when comparing role sets -- correctly, since a
single-example 'missing' verdict over a construct no example declares carries no
information. The skip used to be silent, and silence is the defect these records
close: a generator no reference example reaches has no end-to-end signal at all,
and nothing distinguished 'no example CAN reach this' from 'no example HAPPENS
to'. Every skip now carries a status and a reason, and the gate fails on an
unrecorded pair AND on a record whose pair is no longer vacuous.
The three statuses are never interchangeable -- each carries a different remedy:
unreachable-by-design  No reference example can produce a matching file at
all, whatever it declares and whatever it targets;
something outside the example's control gates the
emission. Adding an example is never the remedy.
cloud-platform-only    Reachable only by an example whose deployment profile
resolves to a cloud provider. Every example resolves
provider = "local" (108 declarations across the example
configs; zero aws/azure in any profile of any example),
so this is not a missing DSL block -- it is the corpus
having no cloud-targeting example at all, which would
swap that example's ENTIRE infrastructure output.
unexercised            Reachable under the corpus's own local/docker shape;
no example declares the triggering construct. Ordinary
corpus-coverage debt, closed by one DSL addition.
Never close a record by weakening the language's declaration. Deleting a domain's
structural_pattern so the census stops seeing it only turns the vacuous role into a
missing one, which the gate then fails; it is not a fix.
Every reason below was established by reading the gating code and by running the
stated matcher against a known instance first, so an absence count is evidence
rather than a matcher that silently matches nothing.

records.reason: Pattern */src/*/infrastructure/cdn.py. CDN-module emission requires all three of: the resolved platform realizing CDN cache invalidation, a declared cdn block, and that block enabled (datrix-codegen-kernel/src/datrix_codegen_kernel/platform/cdn_emission.py, service_needs_cdn_module). provides_cdn_cache_invalidation is True only on the aws and azure platform capability declarations; azure-vm declares it False and the local docker target does not declare it at all. Both preconditions are missing from the corpus: zero cdn blocks in the 201 example .dtrx files (matcher proven against datrix-language's cdn-*.dtrx transformer fixtures), and every example config resolves deployment.provider = "local". Closing this needs the corpus's first cloud-targeting example, not a cdn block.

Pattern */src/*/clients/*_models.py -- the per-extern-service models module ExternClientGenerator.generate_models emits (datrix-codegen-python/src/datrix_codegen_python/generators/extern/extern_client_generator.py:480) alongside its client/errors/contracts. The gate for the whole family is extern_service_dependencies(service) (same file, line 297), which reads service.uses_directives and keeps only ExternService targets -- never service.depends_on(), which structurally excludes them. No reference example declares an extern service: zero matches across all 201 example .dtrx files, with the same matcher finding the real declarations in datrix-codegen-typescript/tests/fixtures/system-full-domain-surface.dtrx. Nothing platform-gated stands in the way -- an extern service is wired on the local docker target. Because no example declares an extern service in ANY language, no language's generated footprint contains a real extern client. This coordinate was invisible until the pattern was suffix-scoped: the former directory-wide */src/*/clients/*.py matched 236 generated paths (at the time of the measurement), every one of them emitted by micro_generators/resilience.py ({dep}_client.py, resilient_client.py, resilience_metrics.py), generators/api/response_struct_generator.py ({dep}_responses.py), or the clients package __init__.py, so the domain read as corpus-realized off another domain's output. The remedy is one extern service declaration plus a uses directive in an existing example, not a pattern change.

Pattern */src/*/models/*/soft_delete_cascade_listeners.py names the soft-delete CASCADE file family, which is driven by the onSoftDelete relationship modifier (datrix-common/src/datrix_common/datrix_model/entity.py, Relationship.has_soft_delete_cascade -> has_modifier("onSoftDelete"); consumed by build_soft_delete_cascades in datrix-codegen-common/src/datrix_codegen_common/algorithms/entity_relationships.py). The corpus DOES exercise the SoftDeletable trait -- 31 declarations across the example .dtrx files -- but declares the onSoftDelete modifier zero times, and the same matcher finds it in datrix-codegen-python/tests/fixtures/soft-delete-cascade.dtrx and datrix-codegen-typescript/tests/fixtures/soft-delete-onsoftdelete-cascade.dtrx. The remedy is one `: onSoftDelete` modifier on an existing hasMany between two entities that already carry `with SoftDeletable`; no platform dependency.

Pattern */src/*/middleware/tenant_middleware.py. No reference example declares the Tenantable entity trait: zero matches across the example .dtrx files, with the same matcher finding the trait in datrix-language's own builtins.dtrx. No example config declares a tenancy { identifier { ... } enforcement: ... } block either: zero matches across the example .dcfg files, with the same matcher finding real tenancy blocks in service configs outside the corpus. Nothing platform-gated stands in the way. The remedy is one entity gaining `with Tenantable` plus a tenancy block in that service's config.

Both preconditions are missing from the corpus: zero cdn blocks in the 201 example .dtrx files (matcher proven against datrix-language's cdn-*.dtrx transformer fixtures), and every example config resolves deployment.provider = "local".
